teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: introduce, meet, family, picture, photo, how many, who, relationship, couple, married, single

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
introduce, meet, family, picture, photo, how many, who, relationship, couple, married, single
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Let me introduce my colleague (formal introduction)
• Do you have any brothers or sisters? (asking about family structure)
• This is a photo of my family (showing photos)
• Are you married or single? (asking marital status)

teacherNotes.title: Phonetic Focus
teacherNotes.content: Rising intonation in yes/no questions ('Do you have brothers?'). Falling in Wh-questions.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus:
Rising intonation in yes/no questions ('Do you have brothers?'). Falling in Wh-questions.

teacherNotes.title: Grammar Function
teacherNotes.content: Question Formation (Who, How many, Do you have...?) + Demonstration structures (This is..., These are...)

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Question Formation (Who, How many, Do you have...?) + Demonstration structures (This is..., These are...)
Controlled Practice:
You want to introduce your colleague to your boss. What do you say?
Reading Script & Dialogue:

A: Let me introduce my friend, Elena.
B: Nice to meet you, Elena! Are you married?
C: Nice to meet you too! No, I am single, but I have a big family.
Listen to introductions at a social gathering and note questions about family and relationship status.

teacherNotes.title: Speaking Aim (~70%)
teacherNotes.content: Practice speaking with your partner: I can introduce someone to others and ask questions about another person's family and social circle.

elements.content: Communicative Speaking Task:
